# VAGEN: Reinforcing World Model Reasoning for Multi-Turn VLM Agents

> VAGEN (arXiv:2510.16907, NeurIPS 2025) is a multi-turn reinforcement learning (RL) framework that trains VLM agents (vision-language model agents) to reason with an internal world model through explicit visual state reasoning. Authors: Kangrui Wang*, Pingyue Zhang*, Zihan Wang*, Yaning Gao*, Linjie Li*, Qineng Wang, Hanyang Chen, Chi Wan, Yiping Lu, Zhengyuan Yang, Lijuan Wang, Ranjay Krishna, Jiajun Wu, Li Fei-Fei, Yejin Choi, Manling Li (* equal contribution; Manling Li is the corresponding author). Affiliations: Northwestern University, University of Washington, Stanford University, Microsoft, University of Wisconsin-Madison, UIUC.

VAGEN combines world models with agentic reinforcement learning for VLM agents: instead of rewarding only task success, it architecturally enforces and rewards the agent's world model reasoning itself. The problem is formulated as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), and the agent's reasoning is decomposed into State Estimation ("what is the current state?") and Transition Modeling ("what is next?").

## Key facts

- A 3B-parameter VLM agent (Qwen2.5-VL-3B backbone) trained with VAGEN-Full reaches an overall score of 0.82 across five visual agent tasks: Sokoban, FrozenLake, Navigation (3D embodied navigation), PrimitiveSkill (robot object manipulation), and SVG Reconstruction.
- The untrained Qwen2.5-VL-3B scores 0.21 on the same tasks (an absolute gain of 0.61).
- The paper's abstract compares this with proprietary reasoning models: GPT-5 (0.75), Gemini 2.5 Pro (0.67) and Claude 4.5 (0.62). Table 2 of the paper lists Claude 4.5 Sonnet at 0.64.
- Five reasoning strategies are compared: NoThink, FreeThink, StateEstimation, TransitionModeling, and WorldModeling (StateEstimation plus TransitionModeling). With RL alone (VAGEN-Base), WorldModeling scores 0.76 overall, versus 0.67 for FreeThink and 0.28 for NoThink.
- The best internal state representation is task-dependent: natural language works best on Sokoban (0.61) and FrozenLake (0.71), while a structured format is slightly better on PrimitiveSkill manipulation (0.94 vs 0.91).
- Two algorithmic components make up VAGEN-Full: (1) the WorldModeling Reward, a dense turn-level reward in which an LLM-as-a-Judge compares the agent's <observation> and <prediction> reasoning with ground-truth states; (2) Bi-Level GAE, turn-aware credit assignment that computes turn-level advantages first and then token-level advantages within each turn.
- Policy optimization uses PPO with observation tokens masked out of the loss. RL baselines with the same backbone: Vanilla-PPO 0.26, GRPO with mask 0.54, Turn-PPO with mask 0.55.
- Accepted to NeurIPS 2025.

## Related work

Unlike RL frameworks built for text-based LLM agents (such as RAGEN) or single-turn visual reasoning RL (such as VLM-R1), VAGEN targets reinforcement learning for multi-turn VLM agents under partial observability, where the agent must reason explicitly about visual states and how they change.

## Common questions

### What is world model reasoning in VAGEN?

It is the agent's own reasoning text about the environment, not a separate world model network. Before each action the VLM agent writes StateEstimation in <observation> tokens and TransitionModeling in <prediction> tokens; together these form WorldModeling. RL rewards this reasoning through the WorldModeling Reward.

### Is VAGEN agentic reinforcement learning (agent RL)?

Yes. VAGEN trains agents through multi-turn interaction with environments, optimizing the policy with PPO and assigning credit across turns and tokens with Bi-Level GAE.

### Is VAGEN RL for vision?

Yes. It is reinforcement learning for vision-language models acting as agents: every observation is an image, so the agent must estimate the visual state and predict how it will change.

### What are multi-turn VLM agents?

VLM agents that act over many turns, receiving a new visual observation after each action. VAGEN treats this as a POMDP, because a single image only partly reveals the true state.

### How does VAGEN relate to RAGEN and RAGEN-2?

RAGEN (arXiv:2504.20073) studies multi-turn RL for text-based LLM agents. VAGEN extends agentic RL to visual observations and adds world model reasoning. RAGEN-2 ("RAGEN-2: Reasoning Collapse in Agentic RL", arXiv:2604.06268, https://ragen-ai.github.io/) is a later MLL Lab paper on template collapse in agentic RL, where reasoning looks diverse but does not depend on the input.

### How does VAGEN relate to ViewAgent?

ViewAgent ("Planning with the Views", arXiv:2605.29563, https://viewagent.github.io/) is a later MLL Lab project on view planning with multi-turn VLM agents in real ScanNet scenes. VAGEN rewards the VLM agent's internal world model reasoning through RL; ViewAgent builds a view-planning environment and benchmark (ViewSuite) with full 6-DoF camera control.

### How does VAGEN relate to Embodied First Exam?

Embodied First Exam (EFE, https://www.embodied-first-exam.ai/) is a later MLL Lab release, a benchmark of frozen robot tasks that coding agents answer with programs. It is a website, code repository and report, not an arXiv paper. VAGEN trains VLM agents with RL; EFE evaluates coding agents on robot tasks.
